shortlist: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of a pruritic, erythematous papular and macular eruption, initially classified as a grade I rash, are more consistent with an acneiform eruption, especially given the initial response to hydrocortisone and the lack of systemic symptoms such as eosinophilia or liver enzyme elevations.

rejected.label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome
rejected.why: No eosinophilia or liver enzyme elevations

rejected.label: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)
rejected.why: Same reasoning as DRESS syndrome, and lower score

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP)
rejected.why: Lack of pustules and lower score

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: Not enough evidence of mucosal involvement or severe skin detachment
